A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TrendFact and FactISR. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–J are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original retrieval, verification, explanation-generation, ablation, and efficiency results, plus gold-evidence experiments in Appendix I.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark and ablation results, retains gold-evidence experiments, and adds a resource-constrained evaluation in Figure 4.

M1.justification: FactISR changes from DEA, six-step evidence triangulation, and symbol-triggered reward decoding to DEA with influence-dependent probabilistic self-reflection. The triangulation template disappears, and the revised prompt uses evidence tools and explicit reconsideration, substantially changing inference.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 7,643 Chinese samples from the same trending platforms and CHEF, covering the same five domains and retrieval, verification, and explanation tasks, including gold-evidence conditions. The enlarged evidence pool and resource-budget variations revise settings within this coverage.

E2.justification: GPT-4.1 replaces GPT-4o in the main and gold-evidence comparisons. Main tables also report DeepSeek-V3-0324 and DeepSeek-R1-0528 instead of the earlier unversioned entries. The retrieval comparators, PROGRAM-FC, CLAIMDECOMP, and Qwen/QwQ families remain.

E3.justification: The evidence library expands from 66,217 to 366,634 entries, with construction now reporting key-element decomposition and GPT-4.1. ECS evaluation and risk scoring switch from GPT-4o to GPT-4.1. Ablation and efficiency tables replace accuracy with F1, and the new resource experiment varies evidence counts and reflection intensity.

E4.justification: v4 adds a central resource-efficiency analysis comparing HCPI against evidence counts and inference time for RAG and FactISR (Section 6.3, Figure 4). It removes ET ablations, revises the remaining component analyses, and replaces the cold-wave reflection case with an electricity-price case. Gold-evidence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new resource curves do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main results are extensively replaced: bge-m3 R@5 changes from 78.97 to 39.97, and FactISR(QwQ-32B) F1 changes from 67.58 to 61.17. Changed corpus and method conditions prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance losses. Resource curves and revised case findings are added. Gold-evidence Tables 10–11 retain all numerical scores despite replacing the GPT-4o label with GPT-4.1.

T1.justification: The core formal inference rule changes from additive token rewards in v3 Equation 1 to normalized influence-dependent reflection probabilities in v4 Equation 4. v4 also introduces HPA=f(C,HI,R). ECS levels remain unchanged, and HCPI is largely reformulated, although Appendix F's NEI expression omits the summation present in v3.

C1.justification: The method contribution is redefined from general reasoning enhancement through three components to influence-adaptive reflection that improves hotspot perception and computational efficiency. The introduction explicitly frames HPA around handling high-influence claims and allocating resources. The core Chinese benchmark and ECS/HCPI contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 attributes RLMs' stronger HCPI to reasoning over event attributes; v4 explicitly acknowledges HCPI's dependence on verification accuracy and argues that influence-dependent budgets address excessive or insufficient reasoning. Interpretations of concise RLM explanations and the limitations concerning manual labor costs remain.

D1.justification: The implementation description replaces reward-decoding parameters and the triangulation prompt with tool-call instructions, reflection intensity, normalization epsilon, and a three-reflection cap. v4 newly documents collection rate limits and date precision, but drops the annotator-team composition and explicit 15% missing-hotspot statement. Hardware and the code/data access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting hotspot prioritization, including Solovev and Pröllochs, Sehat et al., and Damasceno et al., and cites WebThinker to motivate limitations of fixed retrieval. FEVER and data-law references are also added. The broader fact-checking benchmark and explanation-generation positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, construction narrative, and method section undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization. v4 adds standalone HPA and ethics sections, brings metric definitions into the main benchmark section, and separates HPA findings from explanation-generation discussion.

P2.justification: The original combined overview is redistributed into a first-page example, a redrawn construction diagram, and appendix distribution charts. The FactISR diagram is redesigned, annotation review is incorporated into the construction diagram, the ECS table moves into the main text, and a new resource-comparison plot is added.

improvement.justification: v4 makes influence-dependent inference more explicit, adds a relevant resource-budget study, and improves collection disclosures. However, central reporting becomes inconsistent: Table 7's Qwen3 times imply a 20.58% reduction, not 30.17%; gold-evidence tables relabel unchanged GPT-4o scores as GPT-4.1 without explanation; and Appendix F omits the NEI summation. These issues obscure the reliability of the revised metric and efficiency evidence, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
